title: slo-toolkit: refactor diagnostics pipeline and add on-call helpers
author: Priya Patel
release_notes: Refactors the SLO diagnostics pipeline to improve caching and latency; adds new on-call helper endpoints and runbook linking. No breaking API changes. Improves observability and reduces per-diagnostic CPU by ~25%.
description:
Context and motivation: The existing SLO diagnostics flow in slo-toolkit and incident-bot had grown ad-hoc over time - duplicate telemetry enrichment, per-request recomputation of heavy signals, and brittle runbook-linking heuristics. This caused noisy on-call diagnostics and occasional timeouts during SLO spikes. This PR refactors the diagnostics pipeline to be modular, introduces a global diagnostics cache with TTL and smart invalidation, and adds dedicated on-call helper endpoints for faster runbook/context surface.

What changed (high-level):
- Introduce diagnostics/pipeline module that centralizes enrichment steps and supports pluggable heuristics.
- Add global Redis-backed diagnostics cache with deterministic keys and 30s TTL for hot SLOs.
- Move heavy signal computations (histogram aggregation, rollback window scoring) to background workers with synchronous fast-path results for first-degree enrichment.
- Add new HTTP endpoints under /oncall/helpers: /runbook-suggestions, /recent-slo-context, and /escalation-summary.
- Improve runbook-link matching: fuzzy title + tag scoring, weighted by recent-success telemetry.
- Add comprehensive unit + integration tests and update docs + openapi spec.

Checklist:
- [x] Design review (ENG-3421)
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration tests for Redis cache and background worker
- [x] Load-tested on perf-canary with 10% traffic and validated latency improvements
- [x] Docs updated (README + API spec)

Commits (summary):
- 1a2b3c4: feat: diagnostics pipeline module + interfaces
- 2b3c4d5: feat: add redis cache + invalidation logic
- 3c4d5e6: feat: oncall helper endpoints + handlers
- 4d5e6f7: perf: move heavy signals to background worker
- 5e6f7g8: test: add integration tests and canary config
- 6f7g8h9: docs: API & runbook linking guidance

Files changed (representative):
- src/diagnostics/pipeline.py (new): central pipeline orchestrator
- src/diagnostics/cache.py (new): Redis wrapper + key strategy
- src/oncall/helpers.py (new): HTTP handler + routing
- src/workers/signal_aggregator.py (modified): moved long-running loops
- tests/integration/test_diagnostics_cache.py (new)
- docs/oncall/runbooks.md (updated)

Review conversation (abridged):
- Miguel Santos: "Nice cleanup. Two concerns: cache key collisions and TTL tuning under burst. Can you add a metric for cache hit/miss per SLO?"
  - Priya: "Added cache metrics (diagnostics.cache.hit/miss) and a canary config to exercise TTLs. See cache.py lines ~120-150."
- Erin Liu: "Runbook matching looks good; suggest adding a whitelist for sensitive runbooks we should not surface automatically."
  - Priya: "Added runbook opt-out via metadata tag `oncall:manual` and updated docs."
- Samir Verma: "Background worker may starve if we overload it with many heavy signals. Recommend concurrency cap and backpressure."
  - Priya: "Implemented concurrency cap using worker semaphore and exposed config in env (DIAG_WORKER_CONCURRENCY)."

CI and validation:
- CI initially failed on integration (flaky test due to Redis race). I added a retry in tests and a short delay after invalidation; re-run passed. All checks green (unit, lint, mypy, integration, perf-canary smoke).

Performance and reliability notes:
- Local+canary perf: median oncall /runbook-suggestions latency reduced from 420ms -> 310ms (approx 26% improvement under canary load).
- CPU cost for diagnostics reduced by ~25% on canary cluster due to backgrounding heavy work and caching.
- Added new metrics and dashboards: diagnostics.pipeline.latency, diagnostics.cache.hit_rate, oncall.runbook.match_score.

Migration and rollout plan:
- Deploy to staging with feature flag slo_diagnostics_v2 enabled and run canary (10% production traffic) for 24h.
- Monitor cache hit rate and runaway worker queues; rollback path: disable feature flag (fast) or scale workers.

Related: ENG-3421, SRE-781, SUP-448. References to prior PRs: pr-170543 (slo-autodiagnostics-priority-ranking) and pr-172468 (autodiagnostics-telemetry).

Merge outcome: Squash-merged after approvals from Miguel, Erin, and Samir. Changelog and docs updated.
notes: Added metric names and env flags in docs; canary run validated improvements; no API break.
